top.title: Mikel Arteta provides injury update on Bukayo Saka while defender set for long-awaited return
top.description: Bukayo Saka looks set for another month on the sidelines -Credit:Alex Grimm/Getty Images Mikel Arteta has confirmed that both Bukayo Saka and Martín Zubimendi will miss Arsenal's Premier League match against Newcastle United. The Gunners travel to St James' Park on Saturday, with Arteta's side sitting five points clear at the top of the table. As they look to extend their impressive run of five consecutive league victories to six, they will be forced to do so without two of their most influential players. Saka continues to be sidelined with the injury he picked up against Bayern Munich, while Zubimendi sustained a knock while on international duty with Spain. Tom Brady linked with Chelsea investment after abrupt Birmingham City exit U.S. Soccer executive opens up on search for Mauricio Pochettino replacement -Credit:Stuart MacFarlane, Arsenal FC via Getty Images Arteta confirmed on Friday that Saka would not require surgery, but the England winger is still facing around a month on the sidelines. He said via The Mirror : "Yeah, so we had another test; he's evolving really well, but it's going to be an eight-week injury, more or less. So I think he's four at the moment, so it's still a while for him to be back with the team. "Martin [Zubimendi] is [also] out. Unfortunately, he has a muscular problem in his hamstring. He wasn't too concerned to be fair after the game, but after the MRI scan shows that there is an injury there, and he's going to be out for a few weeks, I think." While both Saka and Zubimendi are ruled out, William Saliba looks set to return to the squad for the trip to Newcastle. The French defender has been absent with a back problem since the FIFA World Cup, but Arteta confirmed he is ready to be selected, saying: "He's ready. He's in good condition. We want to ramp up his minutes. He played actually two games, one behind closed doors and one more official [the Under-21s], and he did really well and he's in good condition." To listen to the latest episode of 'All Out Soccer' - CLICK HERE Bruno Guimarães was also a topic of discussion, with the midfielder preparing to face the club he left in the summer. Arteta expects a warm reception for the Brazilian, while also confirming that international teammate Gabriel Magalhães returned in good shape following the break. He commented: "Yeah both Gabi and him [Guimarães] came back and the same as the others and they are in good condition and we need to nail the preparation and we know how difficult it is to play against Newcastle. I hope (he gets a good reception), I think he was one of the main players, and he came in a really important part."

top.title: Mauricio Pochettino confirms Bruno Fernandes decision ahead of Liverpool test
top.description: Mauricio Pochettino confirms Bruno Fernandes decision ahead of Liverpool test Bruno Fernandes to Remain Manchester United Captain Under Mauricio Pochettino Mauricio Pochettino has made his first significant call at Manchester United and there is no ambiguity around it. Bruno Fernandes remains club captain. That was the headline from Pochettino’s first media appearance after taking charge at Old Trafford, where he inherits a side in the Premier League relegation zone and a dressing room that has looked unstable for weeks. His first assignment is brutal enough, an away trip to Liverpool, and he arrives with one obvious fire to contain, the future and authority of Fernandes. Bruno Fernandes Role Confirmed The Portugal international has reportedly turned down two contract offers this season. His current deal expires at the end of the campaign, which means from January he can agree a pre-contract with an overseas club and walk away for nothing. For a player of his profile, that is a major issue. There has also been noise around his behaviour. Fernandes publicly questioned his former manager’s tactics after the 4-1 Champions League defeat to Como. He was then dropped for the 3-0 loss at home to Bournemouth, before returning for the 2-0 defeat at Chelsea after talks with Michael Carrick. Photo IMAGO Mauricio Pochettino Sets Immediate Tone Pochettino did what a new manager often has to do, remove uncertainty, at least publicly. “I think the commitment of all the players is amazing from day one,” he said. “Bruno is our captain and he’s a very important player, but all the player must feel they are important. “We chatted yesterday and spent three hours chatting in my office with all the players. I missed some injured players, but in the next few days, I will talk to everyone.” Manchester United Contract Issue Still Open This does not settle the contract stand-off. Pochettino admitted there “would be time” to address Fernandes’ long-term future and avoided making any stronger guarantee beyond the armband. That is sensible. Manchester United need points, order and clarity. Pochettino has started with the easiest message to send. The harder part comes next, winning matches and convincing Fernandes that his future still belongs at Old Trafford.

top.title: Giants Rookie Malachi Fields Proves He Is Ready For More Touches
top.description: Vincent Carchietta-Imagn Images Malachi Fields is not acting like a rookie. Through nine games, the Giants third-round pick has recorded 350 yards and one touchdown by catching 22 of 38 targets. He has yet to drop a pass. This reliability stands out in an offense that often struggles to move the chains. Offensive coordinator Matt Nagy says he is not surprised by the rookie’s steady play. The team traded up to get Fields in April, giving up picks in 2026 and 2027 to secure his spot at number 74 overall. Fields has become a key part of the passing attack behind Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely. He has 10 receptions for 185 yards over his last three games. His big gain came in the recent loss to Washington where he had three catches for 62 yards. The offense looks different now that J.J. McCarthy took over as the starter in Week 7. McCarthy has given Fields more chances to make plays in space. Coaches See High Ceiling Matt Nagy believes Fields has a long way to grow. “Not surprised at all with him,” said offensive coordinator Matt Nagy, according to Sports Illustrated . “You all have heard me talk about him all camp. His ceiling — when we have this conversation five years from now, you’re going to think about this question you’re asking me because he’s really good.” Nagy told reporters on Thursday that the rookie does everything right. He catches the ball, blocks for runners, and makes plays when needed. The coordinator thinks the rookie’s potential will keep getting higher. Nabers agrees with the high praise. He highlighted Fields’ ability to separate from defenders and track the ball in the air. “Yeah, I mean, just giving him the ball in space, I think he gets open pretty well. I think he has good feet for how tall he is, he runs fast, can track the ball well. He gets in and out of his breaks,” Nabers said, according to Sports Illustrated . The veteran receiver is happy to see the team give Fields more opportunities to find his rhythm. Teammates Trust Him in Coverage Isaiah Likely no longer views Fields as a typical first-year player. The tight end sees a teammate who understands how defenses work. “I don’t really look at Malachi as a rookie anymore. I look at him coming into his own,” Likely said, according to Giants Wire . He explained that when defenses focus on him and Nabers, Fields must win his one-on-one matchups. Likely feels the rookie has done a great job of winning whenever he is asked to. Fields knows his role in these situations. He understands that if he gets single coverage, the ball is likely coming his way. “But Malachi’s definitely honed in on knowing that if I get one-on-one coverage, ball is most likely going to me. So I’ve just got to make my play,” Likely said while describing the rookie’s mindset. This awareness helps the Giants offense keep moving even when the other team loads up against the top targets. top.title: Meta reconsiders 2030 net-zero goal amid record emissions from AI data centers
top.description: Meta’s executives are rethinking the company’s original goal of achieving net-zero emissions by 2030. That revelation in Meta’s latest sustainability report comes as the company reported a record percentage increase in greenhouse gas emissions that exceeds any other Big Tech competitor racing to build new AI data centers. The company’s 2026 sustainability report claims that “our long-term ambitions haven’t changed, but our operating environment has,” according to an introduction from Rachel Peterson, vice president of data centers at Meta, and Blair Swedeen, global head of net zero and sustainability at Meta. In the November 19, 2026, report, they attributed the changing conditions and the need for a rethink to how “demand for AI infrastructure has grown faster than almost anyone projected.” “We are re-evaluating our timelines, sequencing, and interim milestones—including the 2030 timeframe for our net zero emissions goal and our near-term intensity targets—so our approach reflects current operating realities while keeping progress transparent year over year,” Peterson and Swedeen wrote in the report. top.description: Thomas Shea-Imagn Images Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor managed only 21 rushing yards on 11 carries during Thursday night’s 26-3 loss to the Houston Texans, according to RotoBaller NFL . The former Wisconsin Badger added six receiving yards on four catches while playing in a game where his team fell behind early and tried to catch up. According to RotoBaller, Taylor did not score double-digit PPR points in three of his four most recent games. The defensive front in Houston made it hard for Indianapolis to move the ball. Taylor gained just 14 yards on his first four attempts and did not find much room after that. His team entered catch-up mode in the second half, which changed how the offense ran the ball. RotoBaller noted that Taylor’s stability in the passing game is a plus, but it is also a double-edged sword because it stems from the quarterback’s inability to attack deep. Jones struggled to get anything going downfield, which kept the offense in short-yardage situations. This dynamic forced Taylor to be a primary target for short passes even when the run game was dead. The result was a player who was essentially phased out of the game plan as the second half wore on. The offense needed a spark, but the game script dictated a pace that did not favor the running back. Week 11 marked a rough stretch for the star back. This trend makes him much more dependent on the game script, especially for a rebuilding Colts squad. When the team is winning, he can carry the load. They stopped the run early and forced Indianapolis to abandon their ground game. Taylor’s 21 yards on 11 carries show a clear lack of room to run. top.title: Driver Adjustments Shift Aim, Cost Strokes For Amateurs
top.description: John (Jack) Power-Imagn Images Many golfers believe fixing their driver requires complex swing changes or expensive new equipment. A recent analysis shows that setup adjustments often yield better results than mechanical overhauls. PGA Tour putting coach Stephen Sweeney identified specific alignment issues that cause players to miss targets consistently. These errors start before the club even moves. The focus shifts from what is in the bag to how the body aligns with the ball. Stephen Sweeney broke down two critical errors that ruin short-game performance. The first mistake involves eye position relative to the ball. “Where your eyes are right now, I tend to see if players’ eyes are inside the ball line; they tend to look out to the right,” Sweeney said. The arrangement forces the putter to travel from inside to out, creating a path that works for full swings but hinders short putts. The fix requires hinging at the waist more to reach a “tabletop” position. Golfers should keep two putter heads of space from the ball to the toe line and bend forward until eyes sit directly over the golf ball. The second error involves a right-aligned putter face at address. Because the eyes were looking from the inside, the writer subconsciously aimed the face right and tried to pull the ball back to the line. Once the eyes moved on top of the ball, lining up the face became much easier. Sweeney showed a clever trick using a phone to check the aim. “Just go ahead and set up and aim your putter face,” Sweeney said. “If I go ahead and set the back of my phone to your putter face, and you come back and look down that line, you can see the face aimed on the right edge.” This visual confirmation helps players understand their true alignment versus their perceived alignment. Correcting these issues changes the entire stroke mechanics. Confidence returned, and more putts dropped after the writer made these two adjustments. Sweeney explained the mechanics clearly: “As the putter goes back, the putter is moving a little on the inside — but pretty square to where you aimed it.” Equipment like the TaylorMade Qi4D driver or Ping irons listed in Golf Monthly reports can enhance performance, but they cannot fix a broken setup. A player might have the best driver in the world, yet if their eyes are inside the line, the ball will miss the target. The relationship between setup and result remains the most consistent factor in golf. The Impact of Alignment on Scoring Alignment errors often go unnoticed because they feel natural to the player. Sweeney’s observations highlight how a small tilt in the eyes changes the entire path of the club. When eyes sit inside the ball, the brain compensates by aiming the face right. top.title: The most important stat was actually injuries in Bayern Munich’s 1-1 draw with FC Köln
top.description: (Photo by Karl-Josef HILDENBRAND / AFP via Getty Images) | AFP via Getty Images Bayern Munich’s 1–1 draw with 1. FC Köln was a pretty remarkable statistical contradiction. Vincent Kompany’s side controlled practically every aspect o f possession, but the numbers suggest that control did not translate into meaningful attacking superiority. Bayern finished with 71% possession, completed 732 passes at a 92% accuracy rate, registered 17 shots, and won five corners without allowing Köln a single one. Bayern also recorded 35 touches in the opposition penalty area compared to Köln’s 22. By most conventional measures, Bayern dictated the match. Match stats pic.twitter.com/NlydmG3YhJ — Bayern & Germany (@iMiaSanMia) November 20, 2026 However, the more important numbers tell a different story. Despite taking 10 more shots than Köln, Bayern managed just one effort on target. Bayern’s expected goals total was only 0.94, less than half of Köln’s 1.98. The visitors also generated five big chances compared to Bayern’s two. Even more frustratingly, Bayern missed two of its big chances, while Köln squandered four. Both teams had opportunities to take all three points, but neither could capitalize enough to secure the victory. Ultimately, Bayern’s problem was not a lack of possessio n or attacking activity. I t was an inability to turn territorial dominance into genuinely dangerous opportunities while allowing Köln to create considerably better chances with far less of the ball. When you factor in this stat, it tells a little more of the tale for the game: Injuries to Harry Kane and Michael Olise: 2 A 1–1 draw was the result, but the underlying numbers suggest Bayern Munich should have been much better. top.title: Blues’ Three Surprises Prove This Season Is No Fluke
top.description: Charles LeClaire-Imagn Images The St. Louis Blues started the 2026-27 season with a 10-9-2 record, a mark that suggests a team stuck in the middle of the pack. These are lucky breaks and genuine shifts in the team’s identity that could carry them through a long winter. The Goalie Who Stole the Job Joel Hofer has taken the starting net and refused to let go. He is playing well and among the best in the entire league at stopping goals that should have gone in. MoneyPuck states that Hofer’s 8.2 Goals Saved Above expected ranks third in the NHL among goalies who have played 15 or more games. That number is wild for a team that often struggles to score. He has become the backbone of the franchise, and if his teammates can finally feed him the puck, he might get serious talk about the Vezina Trophy. A Waiver Wire Miracle Justin Barron arrived in St. Louis after being cut by the Nashville Predators. In just 19 games, he has scored four goals and added nine assists for 13 points. He also owns a stellar 55.36 expected Goals-For percentage, which shows he drives play better than almost anyone else on the blue line. A full season of this performance could give Barron a claim to being the greatest waiver claim in franchise history. As noted by Bleedin’ Blue , it would be wonderful for the Blues to possess their own version of “the Florida Panthers claimed Gustav Forsling” story. The team found a top-four defender for pennies on the dollar. The Rookie Who Filled the Void Adam Jiricek was not on the opening night roster, but injuries forced a quick call-up that turned into a success story. He played 17 games and looked like a player ready to stay, even if his point total was low with just one goal and two assists. His on-ice impact was promising for a 20-year-old defenseman, and his 51.58 expected Goals-For percentage at 5-on-5 was a solid mark. He has earned another look should the Blues need someone to fill the backend again. The team now has depth that was missing just a month ago. The Blues are 10-9-2 through 21 games, and three players are contributing in unexpected ways.

top.title: 49ers' Mike Evans ‘going in the right direction,' questionable to play vs. Vikings
top.description: San Francisco wide receiver Mike Evans celebrates a first down during the game between the 49ers and Los Angeles Rams at the Melbourne Cricket Ground stadium in Australia on Friday, Sept. 11, 2026. (Sydney Low/For the S.F. Chronicle) San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Mike Evans (Achilles tendinitis) practiced Thursday for the first time since he left the 49ers' Oct. 19 win over the Washington Commanders. On Friday, asked how Evans felt coming out of it, head coach Kyle Shanahan said he was "a little sore" but "going in the right direction." Evans was listed Thursday as a limited participant, and took part in individual drills during the open viewing portion of practice. He ran routes and caught passes at less than full speed. Shanahan said Evans will again be limited Friday during the 49ers' third practice at the Air Force Academy in Colorado Springs, Colorado. "We're all half-speed," Shanahan said, "so we'll keep him out of one period, and then he'll be limited in the rest." San Francisco will make a decision on Evans' game status "probably tomorrow," according to Shanahan, depending on how he feels coming out of Friday's half-speed practice. The 49ers will have a final walkthrough Saturday morning before they fly to Mexico City for their Sunday night matchup against the Minnesota Vikings. General manager John Lynch said Thursday that the 49ers are being "extremely mindful" of the 33-year-old's long-term availability, and that he has "a chance" to play Sunday. "We're going to do what's in Mike's best interest so that when he's here, we can keep him out there," Lynch said on KNBR. "At least have the best chance of doing that." If Evans does play, he'll no longer be the 49ers' oldest wideout. Trade deadline acquisition Keenan Allen (34) would run routes alongside Evans and tight end George Kittle (33), making for an ultra-experienced and tall primary receiving group for quarterback Brock Purdy . Evans is 6-foot-5, Allen is 6-foot-2 and Kittle is 6-foot-4. "It's always good to have tall guys, but that only matters if they have really good hands," Shanahan said. "Fortunately, that's not the case with Mike and … Keenan." More injury notes: Cornerback Renardo Green (back) came off the injury report Friday after being a full participant at Thursday's practice. Green exited the 49ers' last two games early, and he was questionable entering last Sunday's contest against the Dallas Cowboys, but he has no injury designation this week. On Monday, Shanahan said he believed Green was just dealing with back tightness. San Francisco's other starting cornerback, Deommodore Lenoir, was a full participant all week after being limited last week by a foot issue. Lenoir, who played through the injury Sunday against Dallas, allowed 10 catches for 134 yards and three touchdowns on 17 targets. top.title: Charles Leclerc recalls getting stopped by Las Vegas club security as a teenager
top.description: Motorsport photo Today, Charles Leclerc can headline his own pop-up café at Wynn Las Vegas without waiting in line. Funnily enough, however, back when he first set foot in Nevada, he could not even make it past a nightclub bouncer. Appearing on The Fast And The Curious podcast during 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix week, the Ferrari driver opened up about why Sin City holds a personal place in his memory - including an awkward underage run-in with security long before Formula 1 arrived on the Strip. "Las Vegas was the first place I ever went to in the United States with my father back then," Leclerc recalled, referencing a major karting weekend in the city. "I was maybe 15 or 16, and I remember trying to go into a club for the very first time, and I got stopped by security, and my father had to come and pick me up at the security, which [was] quite embarrassing, but it's a funny memory now." The trip dates back to November 2012 - barely a month after Leclerc’s 15th birthday - when he competed in the SKUSA SuperNationals XVI on a temporary circuit at the Rio Hotel & Casino. Even if his nightlife debut ended at the door, his on-track performance stood out: he qualified on pole position in the TaG Senior class and finished fourth in the final. Read Also: Fan voting opens for the Autosport Awards Leclerc later returned to Las Vegas on vacation with close friends around 2017 or 2018, and laughed when hosts Betty Glover and Christian Hewgill asked if bouncers still gave him trouble. "I do now, I do, yeah. I'm over 21, so I'm all good now," Leclerc joked. He then paused to ask whether newly crowned 2026 World Champion Kimi Antonelli had turned 21 yet, only to realise the 20-year-old Mercedes driver is still barred from Vegas clubs himself. From karting memories to cold-weather challenges Since Formula 1 added the Las Vegas Strip Circuit to the calendar in 2023, the venue has been kind to Leclerc. He took pole position and finished runner-up to Max Verstappen in the inaugural race, followed by back-to-back fourth-place finishes in 2024 and 2025. Charles Leclerc, Ferrari Charles Leclerc, Ferrari "I love city tracks, and by definition I also really enjoy Las Vegas, but it's a particular track because it has such low grip and also the temperatures are so low that it has its own challenges," Leclerc said. On the podcast, he warned that cold conditions remain one of Ferrari’s biggest weaknesses in 2026. Even so, Leclerc made an encouraging start in Thursday night’s rain-hit second practice, clocking third fastest behind Mercedes’ George Russell and Alpine’s Pierre Gasly as Ferrari tries to keep its late-season momentum alive. top.title: Hafley Names Kenneth Grant As Next Startership After Phillips Injury
top.description: Credit: Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images Head coach Jeff Hafley has decided to hand the starting defensive tackle role to Kenneth Grant. This move comes after the team lost Jordan Phillips to a season-ending injury during the week. The decision was made public on Wednesday as the Dolphins prepare for a tough matchup. According to Dolphins Talk , Hafley stated clearly that Grant will immediately be relied upon for a significantly higher number of snaps. The Dolphins face a massive hole in their defensive line after losing three players in a short time. Zach Sieler is already out for the year, and now Phillips and Zeek Biggers are gone too. Phillips is undergoing surgery and both he and Biggers will go on injured reserve. The team must find a way to stop the run without these key veterans. Hafley praised the toughness of the players who are gone but said the team has no time to dwell on the bad luck. Grant Gets The Call Hafley did not hesitate when asked about who would fill the void left by Phillips. He pointed directly to the young talent in the locker room who is ready to step up. “It’s going to be KG’s turn,” Hafley said, using the rookie’s nickname to show his confidence. Grant has been working hard in practice and the coaching staff wants to see what he can do against a top-tier offense. The coach also noted that Keith Cooper Jr. would see more time after joining from the practice squad. Cooper has shown he can handle the speed of the NFL quickly. The new players have to learn the scheme fast because they will play on every down. Defensive line coach Austin Clark is calling these extra meetings “night school” to help them study. They need to understand first, second, and third-down calls plus red zone duties. Hafley gave credit to the group for putting in the extra work to get ready. The defense cannot simplify too much or the offense will exploit them for big gains. Brooks Still Elite Even with the losses up front, the linebacker unit is still performing at a high level. Jordyn Brooks has been a standout player despite the team struggling to win games. Hafley believes Brooks is playing at an elite level that should get him more national attention. “He’s playing at an All-Pro level,” Hafley said, backing up his claim with the player’s consistent play. Brooks has shown he can handle the pressure of a losing season and keep improving his game. The Dolphins will face the Buffalo Bills on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET at Highmark Stadium. Hafley expects the new defensive linemen to step up and make plays for the defense. The coach also mentioned that Kyle McCord has another week of practice to get better before the big game. “I’d expect him to play better,” Hafley said, looking for growth from his young quarterback. The team will see if these changes work when they take the field on Sunday.

top.title: DP World Tour Must Copy PGA Tour’s Koepka Fix To Keep Players Happy
top.description: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images The DP World Tour has opened its gates for LIV Golf players to join in 2027. This move includes stars like Bryson DeChambeau, Jon Rahm, and Joaquin Niemann. Current members worry there will be no room left for them in the fields. The tour can fix this fear by copying the smart play the PGA Tour made with Brooks Koepka this year. When Koepka returned from LIV, the PGA Tour did not take a spot from a regular member. Instead, they added three extra spots to every event where Koepka played. This simple change kept the peace while letting a star compete. The DP World Tour needs to do the same thing next season to avoid angering its own roster. The Koepka Precedent for Field Size The PGA Tour faced a similar problem when Brooks Koepka decided to come back from the rival league. Tour officials knew that just letting him in could upset the players who stayed loyal. They needed a way to let him play without kicking anyone else out of the lineup. The solution was to grow the field size whenever he showed up. In 2026, whenever Koepka joined a field, three additional spots were created for other competitors. Consequently, his participation did not displace any PGA Tour member from an event. His presence genuinely expanded competitive chances for other players. Why Players Worry About the 2027 Season Many golfers are scared that the return of big names will hurt their chances to play. When LIV Golf ceased operations, the question of where those players would go was huge. The DP World Tour supplied a full roster of ex‑LIV golfers competing in its events to address that query. Current members now worry about insufficient field space, and the situation has intensified this concern. The fear is real because tournament fields have a hard cap on how many players can enter. If a new star takes a spot, someone else gets cut. To maintain member satisfaction, the DP World Tour should study the PGA Tour’s approach to Brooks Koepka. The most intelligent action taken by CEO Brian Rolapp and the PGA Tour is what the DP World Tour ought to copy. They realized that adding a player does not have to mean subtracting someone else. By adding spots, they turned a potential conflict into a benefit for the whole field. The DP World Tour could readily implement this strategy during the upcoming season. top.title: Giancarlo Stanton Causing Yankees Major Lineup Problem
top.description: New York Yankees designated hitter Giancarlo Stanton On Nov. 10, general manager Brian Cashman revealed that Giancarlo Stanton would be back with the New York Yankees in spring training, saying, "He's not going anywhere." While the Yankees expect Stanton back, his return is actually causing quite a few problems. Stanton cannot play in the field, meaning he is locked into the designated hitter spot. That is causing problems for Luis García Jr. and Aaron Judge. Last season, Stanton missed most of the year, and García played first base and Ben Rice played designated hitter. With Stanton back, Rice will go back to first base, meaning García will have to go back to playing second base, as he did for his entire career before last season. It would be really easy for the Yankees to just plug García in at second base if it were not for Anthony Volpe. Volpe looked good after his return from being demoted, and he figures to be part of the equation at second base. Ultimately, Stanton's return to the team has a ripple effect that essentially takes at-bats away from García. The only way around it is seemingly moving on from Volpe and giving García the keys to second base. Another option would be to move Volpe to third base full-time and move on from Ryan McMahon. However, as long as McMahon is on the team, the Yankees cannot commit to that plan. However, even if the Yankees were to do that, it's not really an upgrade at third base unless Volpe proves he can actually be a consistent offensive force. Going into the year, having to rely on that is not great. On top of all of that, the Yankees are reportedly exploring the third base market. If they do add an external third baseman to replace McMahon, then they are really in a bind with García's playing time. The easiest solution for the Yankees would be to move on from Stanton, play Rice at designated hitter, play García at first base, play Volpe at second base and then add a real upgrade at third base. Another ramification of Stanton's return is Aaron Judge's health. He missed most of last season, and he is not getting any younger. The Yankees may prefer to get him off his feet to help keep him healthy, but they cannot do that with Stanton clogging the designated hitter spot. top.title: Kane suffers ankle injury as Bayern held by Cologne
top.description: Harry Kane was subbed out early with injury as his Bayern Munich side drew 1-1 at home with lowly Cologne in the Bundesliga on Friday. Bayern Munich forward Harry Kane was subbed out with injury in his side's 1-1 draw with Cologne on Friday. (Karl-Josef HILDENBRAND) Tottenham loanee Mikey Moore scored before Kane's injury but Bayern levelled things up when Nathaniel Brown scored before the break. El Mala had an excellent late chance to snare a first Cologne win at Bayern since 2009 but he pulled the ball just wide with the goal beckoning. Now a point behind Bayern, chasers Borussia Dortmund can move into outright first on the table if they win at Borussia Moenchengladbach on Saturday. Bayern also lost Michael Olise to injury in yet another injury blow for the undermanned side. Bayern welcomed coach Vincent Kompany back after a month-long absence and midfielder Jamal Musiala after two months out on Friday, but are already without Luis Diaz, Serge Gnabry, Alphonso Davies, Ismael Saibari and captain Manuel Neuer. Despite the draw Bayern, who play away at Lille in the Champions League on Wednesday, remain the only undefeated side in Europe's top-five leagues in all competitions this season. Kompany returned to the dugout with his arm in a sling, having dislocated his shoulder when he collapsed on the training pitch before being hospitalised with meningeal irritation in October. Cologne, who arrived in Munich with just one league victory this season, took a surprise lead with 12 minutes gone when Moore started and finished an excellent counter-attack. Moore pounced on a mislaid Olise pass and drove forward, finding Linton Maina who laid off for El Mala. With Bayern's defence closing in, El Mala stroked a no-look backheel in Moore's path and the Spurs loanee coolly rounded goalkeeper Jonas Urbig and slid the ball home. Bayern went on the attack immediately but suffered another setback when Kane was brought down in the Cologne box from behind by defender Joel Schmied. Having his penalty appeals waved away, Kane rose gingerly and tried to continue, but was visibly limping and was subbed out soon after. With Cologne sitting deep, Bayern attacked from a distance and broke through before the break when Brown sliced a low shot into the bottom right to level the scores. The hosts suffered another blow in the dying stages of the opening half when Olise went down under a challenge. The France winger did not return to the field after half-time and was seen leaving the stadium shortly after on crutches. Sensing a first victory over Bayern since 2011 -- a run of 23 games including 21 defeats -- Cologne continued to push, with El Mala and Maina forcing a spectacular double save from Urbig just before the hour mark. El Mala had a golden chance to put Cologne in front with eight minutes to go when one-on-one with Urbig but cut his close-range shot inches wide of the post. dwi/dmc

nigeria.description: By Dickson Omobola African Action Congress (AAC) presidential candidate Omoyele Sowore, Friday, faulted the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), saying he will abolish the scheme if elected. Sowore promised to introduce N100,000 grants per semester for students, saying the scheme would provide financial support without requiring repayment. He made the promise during a live session on his Facebook page, adding that students should not be burdened with debt while pursuing their education. He said, “The NELFUND that this government has put in place. First, our party is going to abolish NELFUND. We will turn it into grants.” He added that the policy would replace the existing student loan arrangement. He said, “We are going to give N100,000 per semester, which is N20,000 more than what they are getting now. For two semesters, you get N200,000 so that you can focus on your studies.” Sowore argued that Nigeria should avoid introducing a system that could leave graduates struggling with debt, particularly in a country where employment opportunities were limited. Citing his experience in the United States, where he said he spent 20 years, the AAC candidate described student loans as a source of financial hardship for many graduates. He said, “The biggest cause of depression in America is student loans. Where are you going to get the employment to pay back the loans? But the truth is that even the loans they are giving to them now, they are not paying back. So it just makes sense to turn it into grants.” Sowore said a student completing a four-year program would receive a total of N400,000 under the proposed arrangement, assuming two semesters per year. He described the amount as a reasonable investment in young Nigerians who would contribute decades of service to the country. The former presidential candidate also proposed scholarships for students with outstanding academic abilities, saying beneficiaries could be sponsored to study abroad. “Grants for anybody, whether… scholarships for people who show exemplary ability. He recalled that during his childhood, free education and community efforts to ensure school attendance made education a priority. nigeria.title: I Would’ve Advised El-Rufai To Talk Less If I Had Had Contact With Him — Yahaya Bello
nigeria.description: Former Kogi State Governor, Yahaya Bello, has said he would have advised former Kaduna State governor, Nasir El-Rufai, to speak less if he had had the opportunity to speak with him before his legal battle began. Bello, who spoke during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Friday, said he would have urged El-Rufai to talk less, remain in the All Progressives Congress (APC) that he helped build, and wait to see what President Bola Tinubu would do. He described El-Rufai as a respected and idealistic person who pursues whatever he believes in. Bello said that though he does not wish him “to go down the drain,” the embattled former Kaduna governor must have learnt how to handle political differences. El-Rufai is facing legal battles involving the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) and the Department of State Services (DSS), alongside allegations of financial misconduct and unlawful phone interception. In October, the Court of Appeal dismissed his appeal against the refusal of bail in the alleged financial misconduct case, upholding his continued detention by the ICPC. In a separate DSS prosecution over alleged unlawful interception of National Security Adviser Nuhu Ribadu’s telephone communications, the Federal High Court on October 26 dismissed his no-case submission and ordered him to enter his defence, adjourning proceedings to November 25. The Kaduna corruption trial, involving an alleged ₦8.68 billion CCTV contract, was adjourned to December 8, while a ₦1 billion fundamental rights suit against the ICPC, police and AGF is scheduled for judgment on December 2. nigeria.title: Oyedele urges banks to prioritise agricultural lending
nigeria.description: …Commissions Moniepoint Abuja branch By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief The Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, has urged banks and other financial institutions to make loans more affordable and accessible to businesses, particularly those operating in the agricultural sector, to stimulate productivity and economic growth. Oyedele made the call on Friday at the commissioning of the Abuja branch office of Moniepoint Microfinance Bank (MFB). He said access to affordable financing remained a major challenge for small businesses, stressing that interest rates, fees, repayment periods and the time required to secure loans must be considered in determining the usefulness of credit facilities. “We also must make business finance more affordable and more useful for many small businesses. The challenge is obtaining finance at a cost and on terms that they can sustain. “Affordability involves the interest rates, the fees that we charge, the repayment period, and time spent securing even that facility itself. All of these decide whether financing helps a business or puts it under strain,” he said. The minister said while the government had a responsibility to strengthen economic conditions to make financing more affordable, financial institutions must also contribute through efficient operations, improved risk assessment and transparent pricing. He particularly emphasised the need for increased lending to agriculture, noting that every segment of the value chain required adequate financial support. According to him, farmers need timely access to inputs and working capital, aggregators require funds to purchase produce, while processors need financing for equipment, storage and reliable supplies. He added that transporters and traders also required financial support to move agricultural products efficiently to consumers. Oyedele said appropriate financing for the sector would boost food production, reduce post-harvest losses, improve rural incomes and create employment opportunities. He, however, cautioned that agricultural lending must reflect the realities of farming, including production cycles, weather conditions and market risks. “Repayment schedules should follow production and harvest cycles. Lending decisions should recognise risks such as weather and market conditions, and partnerships with cooperatives, insurers, buyers and other credible participants can help lenders understand and manage them better,” he said. The minister urged Moniepoint to deepen its engagement with agricultural businesses and develop practical partnerships to support viable enterprises. nigeria.title: Tinubu focused on next generation, not next election, Owan-Enoh says
nigeria.description: …Targets APC victory in all 18 Cross River LGAs By Ike Uchechukwu, Calabar The Minister of State for Industry, Senator John Owan-Enoh, has said President Bola Tinubu is focused on building a prosperous future for Nigerians rather than seeking victory at the next election. Owan-Enoh stated this on Friday at Ikom Township Stadium during the inauguration of the Cross River chapter of Project Beyond’s executive and polling unit structures for the Central and Northern Senatorial Districts of the state. He described Tinubu as a pragmatic leader whose decisions were driven by long-term national development rather than immediate political considerations. The minister likened the President’s leadership approach to that of Singapore’s founding Prime Minister, Lee Kuan Yew, whom he credited with transforming the Asian country into a global success story. “That Prime Minister didn’t look at politics the same way a politician looks at the next election. That Prime Minister looked at the next generation. “That is what President Bola Tinubu is doing,” he said. Owan-Enoh acknowledged that the President’s economic reforms had subjected many Nigerians to hardship but described the sacrifices as temporary measures necessary for economic recovery. He likened the reforms to bitter medicine that would eventually restore the country’s economic health. “That tablet is bitter. But after that bitterness, you’ll get well,” he said. According to him, Nigeria has begun experiencing economic recovery and stability after three and a half years of the administration’s policies. He said the government’s next priority was to translate the gains into prosperity and improved purchasing power for Nigerians. “Three and a half years later, recovery has started. Stability has set in, and I think for President Tinubu, the next concentration is prosperity. “The next concentration is the power of your pocket,” he said. The minister further claimed that inflation had declined to about 14 per cent, expressing optimism that it would continue to fall towards single digits. He urged Cross River residents to support Tinubu’s re-election, arguing that the state needed to maintain its influence in national decision-making. “You will need to sit at the table when decisions are taken for you to be able to put before that table what you want,” he said. Owan-Enoh said securing the state’s political relevance required a strong electoral showing for the APC in the 2027 general elections. Recalling the 2023 presidential election, he said Tinubu won in seven of Cross River’s 18 local government areas. He, however, challenged party members to work towards securing victory in all 18 local government areas in the January 16, 2027 presidential election. “In 2023, out of 18 local governments, the President won seven. “In 2027, we must leave here with a determination and a resolve that, come January 16, 2027, Mr President is going to win 18 over 18 in Cross River, and that is possible,” he said. nigeria.description: By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo As the week-long activities to usher Governor Ademola Adeleke’s second term in office took off with Jumat service, the governor has vowed not to disappoint the people of the State. Represented by the Deputy Governor, Prince Kola Adewusi, at the Oja Oba Central mosque in Osogbo, the Governor recalled the struggles and battles for the sustenance of democracy in Osun State and vowed to continue to place the interest of the public at the heart of his administration. A statement issued by his spokesperson, Olawale Rasheed, on Friday stated that the governor commended Osun people for their steadfastness, perseverance and persistent solidarity during the electioneering period, saying the state has become a national model, a symbol for people’s power as the foundation of democracy. “I won’t disappoint Osun people. I will deliver even more than my first term. I am hopeful our financial situation will soon improve with the expected resolution of the local government crisis. We will take good care of workers and all segments of the society,” the governor was quoted as saying. Earlier in his sermon, Sheikh Moruf Ishola described the recent Osun election as “unprecedented in many respects and a standout record for all students of democracy. According to him, the Osun election that re-elected Governor Adeleke broke all records in terms of its dynamics and colours, adding that “the August 15 polls defied all calculations because almighty Allah ran it. “That is why Mr Governor must not abandon God and the people. nigeria.title: UNICEF, Lagos raise alarm over threats to children’s rights
nigeria.description: …As children demand free education, protection, greater say in policies By Chioma Obinna The United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF) and the Lagos State Government have called for stronger protection of children’s rights, warning that their welfare and fundamental rights are increasingly under threat and require concrete government action. The call was made on Friday during the commemoration of the 2026 World Children’s Day at the UNICEF Lagos Office, with the theme, “My Day. My Rights. My Future.” UNICEF Chief of Field Office, Lagos, Celine Lafoucriere, said children’s rights were facing growing threats globally, stressing the need for governments and other stakeholders to guarantee every child access to education, healthcare, good nutrition, clean water, sanitation and social protection. “Children’s rights are under pressure, they’re under threat, they’re being increasingly threatened throughout the world,” she said. Lafoucriere said UNICEF was working closely with the Lagos State Government to ensure that children’s rights were respected and accessible to all, particularly the most vulnerable. She emphasised the importance of social protection programmes, noting that the existence of rights did not automatically translate into access to basic necessities. “Having a right is one thing, but it’s not going to put food on the table,” she said, explaining that social protection interventions could help vulnerable children access education, healthcare and adequate nutrition. She added that Nigeria’s future depended largely on the attention and investment devoted to children today. “The child is the future, and the future of Nigeria is today,” Lafoucriere declared. The Lagos State Commissioner for Youth and Social Development, Mobolaji Ogunlende, said the government remained committed to promoting the welfare, protection and development of every child but acknowledged that it could not achieve the objective without the support of other stakeholders. He urged parents, schools, communities, development partners and other stakeholders to work together to create an environment where every child felt safe, valued and heard. “We must translate what we hear today into meaningful action and commitment,” he said. Ogunlende assured the children that their contributions and concerns raised during the celebration would not end with the event but would inform government policies and practical interventions. nigeria.description: …Calls for prioritisation of Nigerian fabrics, investment in local production By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo The Ooni of Ife, Oba Adeyeye Ogunwusi, has called on the Federal Government to revive and protect Nigeria’s textile industry as part of efforts to strengthen the nation’s economic growth and development. The monarch also urged textile unions to deploy all necessary measures to safeguard the industry and encourage the patronage of locally produced fabrics. Oba Ogunwusi, represented by Olori Aderonke Adeyeye, made the call on Friday at the 38th Annual National Education Conference of the National Union of Textile, Garment and Tailoring Workers of Nigeria (NUTGTWN) and the Nigeria Textile, Garment and Tailoring Employers’ Association in Ile-Ife, Osun State. Commending the unions for organising the conference to educate their members, the monarch said an informed labour union was essential to the survival of democracy and the development of the nation. He said stakeholders must work together to restore the country’s textile industry, revive moribund mills and make locally manufactured fabrics a source of national pride. “It is important for stakeholders to protect our industry. nigeria.title: 2027: Court sacks ADC governorship candidate in Adamawa
nigeria.description: The Federal High Court in Abuja on Friday ordered the removal of Tukur Ribadu as the 2027 Adamawa governorship candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC). Justice Obiora Egwuatu, in a judgment, held that Mr Omar Suleiman, who won the majority of the valid votes cast in the primary election of the party, was unlawfully substituted by Ribadu. Justice Egwuatu ordered the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to immediately restore Suleiman as the rightful candidate of the party. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that Suleiman, a cousin of former Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF), Babachir Lawal, was said to have initially emerged as the ADC’s candidate in the Adamawa primary. However, he was later replaced by Ribadu. Dissatisfied, Suleiman filed a suit marked FHC/ABJ/C’S/1751/2026 before Justice Egwuatu to challenge his unlawful substitution. He prayed the court to order the ADC to forward his name to the electoral umpire as a valid candidate of the party. He also prayed the court to compel INEC to publish his name as the candidate of the party. Delivering the judgment, Justice Egwuatu held that Suleiman could only be replaced as a candidate if he had formally and voluntarily withdrawn from the race or died. He ruled that since Suleiman had neither withdrawn nor died, his replacement was illegal, null and void. The judge consequently ordered INEC to immediately restore his name as the ADC governorship candidate for Adamawa State in the forthcoming governorship poll. nigeria.title: Vandalism, illegal connections threaten Kano water supply
nigeria.description: Over 45 pipeline repairs completed, says commissioner By Hadiza Yusuf KANO — The Kano State Government has warned residents against vandalism, illegal connections and other activities capable of damaging public water infrastructure and disrupting the supply of drinking water across the state. The Commissioner for Water Resources, Dr Dahiru Muhammad Hashim, gave the warning at a press conference in Kano on Friday while briefing journalists on the progress of ongoing rehabilitation of water facilities and restoration of supply to communities. Hashim said the ministry had identified cases of unauthorised connections to water pipelines, vandalism, indiscriminate drilling around major water lines and improper handling of distribution valves. He added that some water pipes had also been damaged by construction activities, refuse burning and other activities around drainage channels. “We appeal to the general public to cooperate with the Ministry in protecting water infrastructure. Our assessment has identified cases of unauthorised tapping of pipelines, vandalism and damage to pipes crossing drainage channels,” he said. The commissioner urged residents, contractors and those executing construction, road and drainage projects to consult relevant authorities before embarking on activities that could affect water pipelines. He also called on residents to promptly report burst pipes, leakages, suspected vandalism and illegal connections to the appropriate authorities. According to him, the restoration of water supply has exposed weaknesses in some old pipelines, many of which had remained without regular water flow for several years. He explained that the return of water pressure to the distribution network had resulted in leakages and pipe bursts in some locations, necessitating urgent repairs and replacement of damaged infrastructure. Hashim disclosed that the ministry had completed more than 45 repair and replacement interventions across different parts of the metropolis. The affected areas include Goron Dutse, Jakara, Kofar Ruwa, Kurmi, Dukawa, Kofar Wambai, Fagge, Club Road, Tudun Wada, Gidan Zakka, Gabari, Koki, Mandawari and Sharada. He said the interventions involved replacing damaged asbestos-cement pipes, fixing leaking PVC pipelines, installing valves and repairing faulty connections. The commissioner further disclosed that water had been pumped from Challawa Water Works to the Goron Dutse reservoirs, which have a reported capacity of 42.5 million litres, before being released into the distribution network. He listed communities that had received water to include Goron Dutse, Gwammaja, Jakara, Kofar Mazugal, Muskwani, Kofar Wambai, Mandawari, Fagge, Tudun Wada, Gama, Kofar Ruwa and Alfindiki, among others. nigeria.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The Tinubu Movement for Sustainable Governance Foundation TMS, popularly known as Tinubu Must Stay, has announced plans to establish a National Reform Documentation and Impact Observatory, a public digital policy archive and a possible future presidential library for President Bola Tinubu. Chairman of the Board of Trustees and National Coordinator of the group, Malam Kashifu Inuwa Abdullahi, disclosed this on Friday during the commissioning of its National Secretariat in Abuja. He said the records would start with Tinubu’s years as Governor of Lagos State between 1999 and 2007, then cover policy developments under successive administrations, his national political career and his presidency from 2023. According to him, the archive would span public revenue administration, infrastructure, investment, education, economic management, digital transformation and institutional development. Students, researchers, historians, policymakers and ordinary citizens would be given access to original documents, implementation records, economic data and independent assessments. Inuwa said the library, the observatory and the archive remained long-term aspirations that would need feasibility studies, sustainable funding, proper governance and professional archival standards. “History serves future generations when it preserves evidence, not merely admiration,” he said. He added that the documentation must make room for achievements, implementation difficulties, independent criticism and lessons learned. The announcement came with a membership claim. Inuwa said the group, formally launched on October 1, 2026, had recorded 61,093 validated members within seven weeks across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT). He said the group had representation in 730 of the country’s 774 local government areas, about 94 per cent geographical coverage. Its digital database also captures 4,750 wards and 22,584 polling units. Inuwa said 65 per cent of members, roughly 40,000 people, were aged between 18 and 34, while the membership was 65 per cent men and 35 per cent women. “The most remarkable feature of our membership is its youthful composition. This is not merely a demographic statistic. It places a profound responsibility upon our institution,” he said. nigeria.description: US President Donald Trump on Friday called for chip giant Nvidia to reinstate disgraced former CEO Jensen Huang after he resigned over extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy. “I would love to see him be back. You have one of the truly most brilliant minds in the world, and where is he going to go?” Trump told reporters. “I think that I would love to see Jensen be given a second chance.” Huang resigned last week as chief of Nvidia, a company at the center of the AI revolution, after revelations of an affair with an alleged Chinese spy who may have funneled restricted chips to that country. Reports of at least two further affairs emerged after that initial report, with US intelligence said to be aware of the possibility of the alleged Chinese espionage. Trump defended Huang as “a good man” who “made some bad decisions.” “I’d like to see Jensen make a big apology and go back because he created something with Blackwell,” he said, referring to the most advanced chips designed by Nvidia. The US president also appeared to directly contradict his own treasury secretary, saying he had spoken to China’s President Xi Jinping about Huang during a summit earlier this week. “I did discuss that with President Xi, and he said, ‘Oh, brilliant, brilliant! He’s a brilliant man,'” said Trump. Earlier in the day, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Trump had not discussed Huang with Xi during the meeting in Shenzhen. Trump advocated for Nvidia to take back Huang as their CEO “if they were smart.” Huang has offered to return to the company, a move the chip giant’s board has rejected. Board chair Harvey Jones said in an earnings call this week that “the Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.” – ‘Must stay ahead’ – Earlier, Bessent had spoken at length about the AI race with China in comments to US broadcaster CNBC. Speaking about the Trump administration’s support for the domestic AI sector, Bessent stressed that the United States “must stay ahead” of China in that realm. “Our best protection against the foreign SI and exploits by foreign actors is for our labs to maintain their substantial lead, and in effect, they are our shield against SI,” he said, using the government’s preferred SI, or “super intelligence.” “There’s no turning back on this. nigeria.title: Nasarawa attracts $2.3bn investments in seven years — Abdullahi
nigeria.description: Records 21 reforms, 11 PPP projects worth ₦93bn By John Alechenu ABUJA — Nasarawa State has attracted more than $2.3 billion in investments over the past seven years following reforms and institutional development aimed at making the state more competitive and investor-friendly. The Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of the Nasarawa Investment and Development Agency, Ibrahim Abdullahi, disclosed this at the 13th World Public Relations Forum 2026 in Abuja. Abdullahi said the investments cut across agriculture, solid minerals, retail, commercial activities, manufacturing, agro-processing and education. He added that the state also implemented 11 public-private partnership (PPP) projects valued at about ₦93 billion within the period. According to him, the achievements were the outcome of seven years of reforms and deliberate institution-building under Governor Abdullahi Sule, rather than publicity campaigns or political slogans. Recounting the beginning of the process, Abdullahi said he was invited into the Nasarawa State public service seven years ago, when Governor Sule appointed him as economic adviser. He said the assignment was to develop the state’s investment profile and position it as an attractive destination for investors. He thanked the organisers of the forum for recognising Governor Sule with an honour presented a few days earlier. Abdullahi said one of the first lessons from the assignment was the need to establish the necessary structures before embarking on investment promotion. “So we could not go out and invite people to come to Nasarawa State without building any framework around it. That is to say that you cannot communicate something that is not there. You cannot communicate something that hasn’t been built. So, we put our heads down and began to build,” he said. He explained that the state’s vision, as contained in the Nasarawa Economic Development Strategy, was to make it one of Nigeria’s most competitive states through improved and accelerated economic growth that would translate into better living conditions for residents. Under the strategy, he said, the government implemented more than 21 reforms focused on improving the business environment and making the state attractive to investors. He said the reforms were designed to guarantee a conducive business climate, competitive returns on investment and improved general welfare for residents. According to him, the measures included the digitisation of revenue administration and improvements in the state’s fiscal and financial management framework. Abdullahi said the reforms provided the foundation for the state to confidently promote its investment opportunities to local and international investors. He noted that investors were attracted not by impressive speeches but by predictability, transparency, good returns and a government that honoured its commitments. nigeria.title: The Other Black Gold: Nigeria’s Coffee Sector Wants A Shot
nigeria.description: Richard Ali grew up with the aroma of coffee wafting through his house in central Nigeria as his father, an accountant, worked late into the night, drinking powdered, instant stuff from Maxwell House and Nescafé. It was not until years later, travelling on the other side of the continent, that Ali had a taste of “coffee, coffee — brewed coffee”. “I have to bring this to Nigeria,” he thought, and he started looking into importing beans from Rwanda. Ali later discovered he did not have to: coffee has been growing in Nigeria for more than 100 years. A wave of entrepreneurs in Africa’s most populous country are turning towards the oil-producing nation’s other black gold — an uphill task in a place full of tea and instant coffee, and little sense of homegrown java as a daily staple or part of a wider cultural patrimony. A general view of someone handling coffee beans in a plantation in the Gorongosa mountain range in Gorongosa on May 20, 2022. (Photo by Alfredo Zuniga / AFP) But roasters say they have found a market — and sense of national pride — to tap into, even if Nigeria’s beans are not well-known. “We need to grow more coffee, whether for the domestic market, which is expanding, or the global market, which is now considering Nigerian coffee,” Ali, founder of Tigray Coffee, which launched in 2021, said over a cup of Nigerian brew, light with slightly chocolatey notes. Agricultural Investments In Ethiopia, hundreds of years of cultivation have bound coffee to local culture, while Uganda and Ivory Coast have become modern export powerhouses. Nigeria produced 1,808 tonnes of beans in 2024, according to statistics from the UN’s Food and Agriculture Organisation — a paltry sum compared to Kenya’s 49,500 tonnes that same year. The first seeds hit the ground in Nigeria in the 19th century, after coffee was introduced by British colonists. The crop is notoriously fickle and can only grow in certain parts of the country. But there has also been a dearth of investment in agriculture, critics say, as the government instead became over-reliant on the oil sector for revenues. Experts have long called for a more diversified economy. The government agrees, at least in principle: in May, agriculture minister Abubakar Kyari announced federal investments in coffee production in Ondo State, calling it “a powerful economic crop” that could create jobs and “boost rural livelihoods”. ‘Never Imported Coffee’ At the opening of a new cafe in Lagos last month, Princess Adeyinka Tekenah paired a local brew not with croissants, but puff-puff, a staple street food snack of fried dough. “I have been in the business for 12 years, and I have never imported coffee,” the founder of Happy Coffee said. business.title: SEC Freezes Assets in $560 Million Crypto Trading Ponzi Scheme
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine SEC Freezes Assets in $560 Million Crypto Trading Ponzi Scheme The Securities and Exchange Commission has frozen the assets of Indianapolis-based Backward Hat Capital and its two co-founders, saying the firm ran a $560 million Ponzi scheme that told investors their money would be turned into crypto and used for AI-driven currency trading. The agency said Backward Hat, co-founders Phillip Williams and Devin Johnson, Johnson’s firm Traders Point Capital and Joseph Anderson raised the money from more than 2,000 investors starting in July 2022. A federal court granted a temporary restraining order, an asset freeze and expedited discovery to halt what the SEC called an ongoing scheme. Federal prosecutors in New York and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission brought parallel cases. The SEC and CFTC suits were filed in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Indiana, and the CFTC said the court has appointed Kevin B. Duff as temporary receiver to take control of the companies and the individual defendants’ assets. The pitch: crypto, AI and 6% a month According to the SEC’s complaint , Williams and Johnson sold limited partnership interests in private funds through a network of promoters, including to Williams’s former investment advisory clients. They promised a proprietary, “AI-driven” algorithm that supposedly returned at least 6% every month by trading foreign exchange. Investor money, the pitch went, would first be converted into a crypto asset and then used for that arbitrage. The complaint does not name bitcoin as the asset. It says about $109 million of the roughly $210 million raised from July 2022 to September 2025 was sent to the fund’s Coinbase account and converted. Of that, more than $56 million went to personal crypto accounts held by Williams, Johnson and a relief defendant, according to the complaint. About $40 million ended up on three platforms where some of it was used to trade other crypto assets, but little to no money was used to trade FX. After October 2025, the scheme raised about $350 million, and none of it was sent to Coinbase. Where the money went The SEC said the defendants made more than $250 million in Ponzi payments to earlier investors and moved more than $220 million to themselves. The money paid for exotic cars, expensive homes, private air travel and other businesses they owned, and helped feed Johnson’s gambling. Promoters took more than $50 million. Anderson is accused of producing fake financial reports, including at least two “audit reports” and a “quality of earnings” report from a supposedly independent firm. The SEC said the documents falsely claimed the returns had been verified against bank and brokerage records. It said Anderson did no audit work, was not independent and had a financial stake in the scheme. business.title: Researchers Publish Security Analysis of Bitcoin’s Post-Quantum SHRINCS Proposal
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Researchers Publish Security Analysis of Bitcoin’s Post-Quantum SHRINCS Proposal Several researchers have published a 131-page security analysis of SHRINCS, a proposed post-quantum signature scheme for Bitcoin, and are asking the wider community to look for flaws in it. Researcher Mikhail Kudinov announced the first version Thursday in a thread on X, saying the paper reduces SHRINCS’ security to the properties of its underlying hash function. The analysis, dated Nov. 18, estimates classical security of 121.4 to 122.7 bits for SHRINCS, though those figures rest on assumptions that include three unproven conjectures. Kudinov said the work is not finished. The team is still working on a new analysis of a property called SM-DSPR, whose bound has so far been conjectured, and on tightening a reprogramming step and improving a bound against quantum attackers. How SHRINCS works SHRINCS is a hash-based scheme, meaning its security rests on hash functions rather than the elliptic curve math behind today’s Bitcoin signatures. It places two designs under one key: a stateful part built on FXMSS with WOTS+C, and a stateless fallback built on SLH-DSA. Because both use the same hash function, Kudinov said, the proof has to cover both. Signature size is the main cost. Under the draft proposal, stateful SHRINCS signatures run from 548 to 4,619 bytes, while the stateless fallback is 5,777 bytes. Schnorr signatures on Bitcoin today are 64 bytes, and ECDSA signatures typically come in around 71. Signatures take up scarce block space, so larger ones mean fewer transactions per block. The risk of a stateful signature The compact stateful path carries a danger. It relies on one-time keys, and if a wallet accidentally reuses one, an attacker can forge a signature for that address and steal the funds. Wallet software therefore has to track the state of every key. The stateless path avoids the problem, but at a much larger size. Jonas Nick, Blockstream’s director of research, told Isabel Foxen Duke, head of the MARA Foundation, on MARA Foundation TV that wallets must automatically fall back to the stateless path whenever a state counter could be compromised. “It needs to be impossible for the user to behave in a way that this catastrophic event happens,” he said. “Wallet developers need to deal with this stateful component correctly.” Nick also warned that heavy use of the larger signatures would weigh on the network. “We don’t know what the fee market will look like once we have these very big signatures,” he said. “And it’s not just the fee market, it’s also just fewer transactions fit into a block, meaning fewer people can use Bitcoin. And I think this changes the value proposition of Bitcoin.” Researchers ask for review The authors are clear that the analysis needs scrutiny. business.title: U.S. Treasury Secretary Pushes Back on Bigger Fed Hike
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine U.S. Treasury Secretary Pushes Back on Bigger Fed Hike Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent pushed back Friday on calls for a bigger Federal Reserve rate hike, even as bitcoin broke below $60,000 for the first time since July and stocks sank on bets that the Fed will keep tightening into a selloff. Bessent told CNBC he would encourage the Fed not to embrace a half-point increase at its Dec. 8-9 meeting. He cited the energy supply shock and a drop in crude prices as reasons for the central bank to hold back. Bessent says the Fed should look forward He argued that one governor now backing a 50 basis point hike had wanted a similar cut within the last year. Bessent said it “seems somewhat peripatetic” to want the bigger increase only 11 or 12 months later. He did not name the governor. “I would encourage the Fed to look forward, not backwards,” Bessent said. The comments came two days after Fed Governor Christopher Waller told CNBC a half-point hike is probably necessary in December and that the central bank may need to “shock people.” Waller said inflation is “headed in the wrong direction, and it’s spreading out.” Fed officials split on how far to go Waller is not alone. Minutes of the October meeting showed nearly all officials expect a quarter-point hike in December, and two floated a larger one. Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee also declined to rule out a bigger move on Thursday. “We’ve now had multiple months in a row of borderline disturbingly high inflation rates with little progress in the sectors where we would expect to be seeing some progress,” Goolsbee told reporters. “So everything’s always on the table.” Not everyone wants to go bigger. New York Fed President John Williams said Tuesday that “I don’t think the situation calls for dramatic action.” St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem has suggested as many as four hikes by the spring of 2027. The Fed raised rates in September for the first time in more than three years and held them steady in October. Inflation has stayed hot since the Iran strikes pushed up energy prices earlier this year. Citi and traders still see a quarter-point hike Citi still expects a quarter-point increase in December. Global chief economist Nathan Sheets said Thursday he does not see a need for 50 basis points despite persistent inflation. In a note Friday, the bank wrote that “Fed officials will consequently have little appetite to hike into an equity sell-off.” Citi expects the Fed to hold after December and begin cutting later in 2027. Traders agree on the next step: the CME Group’s FedWatch tool showed a more than 98% chance of a quarter-point hike, and the 10-year Treasury yield fell more than 10 basis points to 4.95% as investors bought bonds. Stocks fell for another day. The Nasdaq Composite dropped more than 2% in morning trading, and the VIX volatility index topped 30 , its highest level since March. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Crashes to $59,000 as Market Selloff Deepens The bitcoin price crashed below $60,000 on Friday for the first time since early July, falling about $1,800 in roughly an hour as a deepening U.S. tech stock selloff dragged risk assets lower. Bitcoin traded near $61,400 at 9:40 a.m. ET and slid to about $59,600 by 10:45 a.m., a drop of nearly 3%, according to Look Into Bitcoin data . The bitcoin price is down about $3,400, or more than 5%, from the same time Thursday, when it traded near $63,000. The break of $60,000 is a key psychological level, and it came with little warning. Bitcoin price had held above $61,000 for most of the morning, even after a third straight daily loss. Stocks and rate hike bets drive the selloff Wall Street opened sharply lower. The Nasdaq Composite fell more than 2% in morning trading as shares of Anthropic extended losses in its second day since a record Nasdaq debut. Nvidia and AMD also traded lower. Bitcoin has been moving with tech stocks. The market has questioned whether heavy spending on artificial intelligence will pay off, and Friday’s open did nothing to ease that worry. Rate expectations are adding pressure. Traders see a roughly 94% chance the Federal Reserve raises rates in December, CME Group’s FedWatch tool showed . Higher rates tend to hurt bitcoin and other assets that pay no yield. Earlier Friday, South Korea’s Kospi index fell more than 5% and chipmakers sank across Asia. That selling carried into U.S. trading and then into bitcoin. Some analysts had flagged $60,000 as a floor. Katie Stockton of Fairlead Strategies told CNBC the bottom of bitcoin’s trading range sits “just below 60,000,” and that it “appears to be trying to find a footing.” Friday’s drop tests that view. CoinShares head of research James Butterfill said this week the drop is a “continuation of the existing bear market.” His base case is range trading around $60,000 to $90,000 through much of 2027. In Asali Africa’s new series, it is where the conversation starts. There’s Rice at Home is a cooking and conversation show from Asali Africa, the Lagos-based creative development agency, hosted by Chef Soliat Bada . In each episode, Soliat cooks one rice dish with a guest, and while the pot does its work, the two get into the kind of talk that usually happens around food: family, money and what success really looks like. Rice is the most ordinary thing in a Nigerian kitchen, and the show makes a good case that it doesn’t have to taste ordinary. Over five episodes, released every two weeks, the menu travels from Jamaica to Saudi Arabia, back home to Nigeria and on to Louisiana. You don’t just watch the food get made, either. The recipes are written up in full on Asali Africa’s website, with the ingredients and method laid out step by step, so you can watch Soliat cook a dish and then make it in your own kitchen. The season opens with Rice and Peas with Oxtail, the Jamaican Sunday staple of rice cooked in coconut milk with red kidney beans (the “peas”), served beside rich, slow-cooked oxtail. Soliat’s guest is Michael Famoroti , co-founder of Stears, and their conversation turns to family and black tax: the expectation that once you start earning, you start supporting the people who raised you. Read the full recipe for Rice and Peas with Oxtail . Rice and peas with oxtail, from Episode 1 Soliat Bada and Michael Famoroti in Episode 1 Episode 2 moves to the Gulf for lamb kabsa, Saudi Arabia’s national dish, fragrant with dried lime and seven spice. Soliat is joined by Bella Adeleke , CEO of Asali Africa and founder of the fashion label Garbe, for a conversation about redefining success. Read the full recipe for Lamb Kabsa . Lamb kabsa, from Episode 2 Still to come are Nigerian fried rice with fried turkey and dodo, cooked with Toyin Jolapamo and Nneoma Mere; jambalaya with Goldie Iyamu and Vanessa Iloenyosi ; and a season finale with Edwin Okolo and Temi Omolehinwa. For more on Asali Africa and the products and ideas it develops, visit asali.africa . Episodes 1 and 2 are out now on YouTube. entertainment.description: “Men are not wired to show emotions.” A male friend once said to me during an argument. He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. Frequent questions men are asked: “How far? Work nko?” “When are you getting married?” “Have you bought land?” “How is the family?” And the famous Nigerian question that can make an unemployed graduate dread family gatherings: “So, what are you doing now?” We often inquire about their achievements, responsibilities, and plans. These aspects are important, but how often do we ask about their fears? A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. A successful professional whose LinkedIn profile showcases numerous achievements, while his personal life tells a story that no one has thought to ask about. We admire their strength, we applaud their sacrifices, and we celebrate their accomplishments. But what about what they are going through? The person everyone leans on also needs somewhere to lean. Society has an interesting checklist for measuring a man’s success. A good job, a house, a car, a wife, children and financial stability. Preferably, all achieved before a certain age. But if a man struggles to achieve all these, is his life any less meaningful? Surely, a man’s worth cannot be reduced to his bank balance, job title or ability to convince everyone that he has everything under control. There must be room for men who are still becoming.
